text.p: Settings for controlling tracing using the GNU Debugger (GDB).
Path to GDB - The path to the GDB executable to use. This could for example be arm-none-eabi-gdb for ARM targets.
Path to image - Optional path to the target image. This may be needed to use symbol names in GDB commands.

Commands to initialize - Commands to send to GDB when the process starts. These are executed for both streaming and snapshot operations. This will typically include a command to connect to a GDB server, like target remote localhost:3333 to connect to a previously started OpenOCD server, or target remote localhost:2331 to connect to a default configured JLink GDB server.
Commands to start stream - Commands sent to GDB to start streaming. This can vary greatly with your setup and will typically include vendor specific "monitor" commands.
Commands to end stream - Commands sent to GDB to end streaming. This can vary greatly with your setup and will typically include vendor specific "monitor" commands.

Trace data is received by - Specifies how to access the trace data.
GDB writes to output specified by $$(TZ_OUT) - GDB will write the trace data to a file passed as argument to one of the commands in Commands to start stream. The command should include the $$(TZ_OUT) macro which will be translated to a unique filename before sent to GDB.
GDB writes to fixed path - Use this when GDB will always write to a fixed path. Configure the path and optional decoding in the PSF settings FileSystem tab.
GDB opens TCP port - Use this when GDB (or more commonly the GDB server) will open a TCP port where the data can be received. Configure the address, port and optional decoding in the PSF settings TCP tab.

Commands to take snapshot - Commands sent to GDB to capture a snapshot. At this time, the command list must include $$(TZ_OUT) and the command should write the contents to that file. The $$(TZ_OUT) will be expanded by the application before sent to GDB. When the target image is specified, you can typically use dump binary value $$(TZ_OUT) *RecorderDataPtr, possibly preceded by monitor halt and if desired followed by monitor resume.

GDB commands are specified one per line and each command will run to completion before the next command can be executed. Lines starting with # will be ignored (never sent to GDB) and can be used for comments. For snapshot and start stream commands, the macro $$(TZ_OUT) will be translated to a unique file name before being sent to GDB.

In addition to GDB commands, there are certain $PNAME commands that will not be sent to GDB but will instead be interpreted and handled by the $PNAME application. These will start with !tz.
!tz wait <timeInMilliseconds> - Will wait timeInMilliseconds before moving on to the next command.
